name: Domestic textured plant protein
what: Dry textured soy protein and soy-gluten granules and slices, made in Vietnam for chay brands, frozen-food makers and co-packers; high-moisture whole cuts as a second step
why_vietnam: Every audited Vietnamese product with 10 g protein or more per 100 g runs on imported textured soy, soy protein or gluten; no commercial extrusion found; buyers named; ordinary food rules
must_be_true: Ex-factory cost at or below landed Chinese textured protein (USD 1.24/kg FOB in 2025; USD 1.29 to 1.38/kg landed; 0% duty under ACFTA and RCEP) (TIC-12; BUY-02; FTR-32); a food-grade, low-temperature defatted soy flour supply below the breakeven price (about USD 700 to 940 per t delivered for a 1 t/h line at 70% utilisation; our calculation, TIC-12; TIC-13); buyers value freshness, customisation and local supply
kill_tests: Delivered food-grade flour costs more than about USD 700 to 940 per t (1 t/h at 70%) or USD 590 to 900 per t (0.5 t/h at 70%); fewer than three buyers sign conditional orders totalling at least 2,000 t a year; Chinese landed price (USD 1.29 to 1.38/kg in 2025) stays below Vietnamese full cost at 2,800 t a year (0.5 t/h at 70%) or 5,600 t a year (1 t/h at 70%), on 8,000 operating hours a year; India-origin textured soy (USD 0.98/kg FOB in 2025) becomes the reference price; Version 0.10: no bank agrees to finance the supplier's receivables against the anchor buyer (supply-chain finance or factoring); without an anchor the working capital of USD 0.6 to 3.5 million has no named source
first_customers: An Nhien, Au Lac, Xuan Hong, LC Foods, Cholimex, CJ Foods Vietnam (Cau Tre, bibigo), Vissan, Thoai An, GN Foods and other co-packers
partners: Extrusion-line suppliers; a soy crusher (VAL) for a food-grade flake stream; FIRI for pilot trials; Version 0.10, finance routes under Vietnamese law (instruments, not recommended providers): receivables finance or factoring against an anchor buyer (Circular 20/2024/TT-NHNN; banks such as BIDV run supply-chain finance for SMEs referred by an anchor company, up to 85% of order value); a finance lease or sale and leaseback of the line from a licensed leasing company (Circular 26/2024/TT-NHNN); and, for an SME owner, a guaranteed loan (the Ho Chi Minh City SME Credit Guarantee Fund caps guarantees at about VND 34 billion, about USD 1.3 million, per customer)
capital_note: Chinese dry-TVP lines of 0.5 to 1 t/h with dryer are listed at USD 11,000 to 100,000 (list prices, TIC-01 to TIC-10); installed capex in Vietnam USD 0.28 to 1.38 million (our calculation); working capital of USD 0.6 to 3.5 million is the larger need; a European-grade line is unverified (USD 2.0 to 5.6 million installed on the v0.1 equipment assumption of USD 1.5 to 4 million). Version 0.4: best owned by a chay maker, co-packer or distributor and financed with debt and trade finance, not venture equity; proposed score changes (capital efficiency 4 to 5, Vietnam advantage 3 to 2) recorded in play_demand_check.csv, scores here unchanged

name: Functional microbial feed ingredients for shrimp and pangasius
what: Yeast, fungal or bacterial biomass products used at 1 to 5% of shrimp or fish diets and sold on survival, feed efficiency or palatability, made on Vietnamese carbohydrate
why_vietnam: Abundant cassava and sugar carbon; captive aerobic fermentation skills; about six firms make most shrimp feed; inactive yeasts already on the livestock feed list; buyers pay for function
must_be_true: Repeatable species-specific trials show at least a 3 to 5% gain in survival or feed conversion at 1 to 5% inclusion; a legal route for aquafeed use (written opinion or trial); cost per tonne of product below the functional willingness to pay (about USD 1,000 to 4,250 per t in total for pangasius; USD 1,280 to 4,800 per t above fishmeal parity for shrimp); delivered price against a revealed bulk inactive-yeast price of about USD 1,100 per t (Vietnam imported about 9,200 t of HS 2102.20 in 2025, 95% at about USD 1.1/kg; FBA-17), or head-to-head trials that show a gain worth the difference
kill_tests: Two independent tank or pond trials fail to show a gain at 5% inclusion or less; Chinese by-product biomass matches the function at a lower price
first_customers: Sheng Long, CP Vietnam, Uni-President Vietnam, Tongwei, Grobest, Gromax (shrimp feed); Vinh Hoan and other integrated pangasius groups
partners: Vedan, Ajinomoto or Daesang (tolling or co-product streams); ShrimpVet or university aquaculture labs for trials; De Heus, GreenFeed, Cargill as distribution
capital_note: Low if tolled on existing tanks; a dedicated plant sits in the fermentation capex range (USD 8,000 to 20,000 per annual tonne, indicative)
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

name: Bulk microbial protein for fishmeal replacement
what: Fungal or bacterial protein made at 10,000 t a year or more to replace 25 to 50% of fishmeal in shrimp feed
why_vietnam: Carbon and buyers exist; the displaceable fishmeal pool is about 120 to 245 kt a year (central), of which 25 to 90 kt in total is realistically contestable by novel proteins, already contested by Chinese microbial protein
must_be_true: Capex below about USD 6,000 per annual tonne (tolling or brownfield); near-free carbon from a side stream; fishmeal stays near its 2026 high; beats Chinese by-product and FeedKind-type imports
kill_tests: After a pilot, measured cost stays above 1.2 times fishmeal-protein parity at 2025 prices; no mill signs an offtake at 70 to 90% of fishmeal-protein parity
first_customers: Shrimp feed makers listed under T2
partners: Starch factories (pulp, wastewater) or amino-acid producers; a DFI for first-loss capital
capital_note: Tens of USD millions for a 10,000 t plant (indicative stack A: capital is 54 to 67% of cost)

name: Cassava starch to fermentation sugar hub
what: Convert part of the cassava starch Vietnam exports into fermentation-grade glucose next to starch factories, and co-locate fermenters (domestic or foreign) at the same sites
why_vietnam: Vietnam shipped 2.15 Mt of cassava starch in 2023, 93.5% to China, while China imported only USD 0.16 million of glucose syrup from Vietnam in 2024; starch factories cluster in Tay Ninh and the Central Highlands; glucose technology is standard
must_be_true: Cassava prices stabilise after the 2025 to 2026 spike and the E10 mandate; at least one fermenter commits to co-locate; wastewater and biogas infrastructure can serve fermentation
kill_tests: No fermenter commits within two years; cassava price volatility makes long-term sugar contracts impossible
first_customers: Domestic food fermenters (yeast, enzymes, koji and fungal foods, amino acids for food); foreign biomass or precision-fermentation food firms seeking a lower-cost ASEAN site
partners: Starch groups in Tay Ninh; provincial investment agencies; industrial parks
capital_note: Not estimated; hydrolysis and refining lines are standard starch-industry equipment

name: Shared pilot and tolling fermentation
what: A food-grade pilot line (hundreds of litres to a few cubic metres) plus negotiated tolling on existing industrial tanks, open to startups and researchers
why_vietnam: Aerobic tanks exist inside Vedan, Ajinomoto and Daesang, but we found no published tolling offer and no open pilot fermenter; startups otherwise scale up in Singapore, Thailand or China
must_be_true: An anchor host (industrial producer, Saigon Hi-Tech Park, FIRI or a university) and an operator; enough users to fill the line; public or DFI co-funding
kill_tests: No host agrees to tolling terms; utilisation below about a third in the first two years
first_customers: Food startups under T7 and T9; research groups; foreign firms testing Vietnamese feedstocks for food ingredients; Version 0.10: YERA (yeast protein, Nghe An) and Emmay (mushroom and mycelium foods) as likely domestic users, and university teaching capstones as an anchor user that fills line time (Berkeley precedent; not costed); ScaleUp Bio (Singapore) and EECi (Thailand) already compete for the same users
partners: Saigon Hi-Tech Park; FIRI; Vedan; Ajinomoto; Daesang; Thai EECi (access arrangement)
capital_note: Pilot scale; public or DFI co-funding expected (not estimated) Version 0.10 benchmark: Metrosert (Estonia) is building an open, food-grade pilot plant with 50 L, 500 L and 5,000 L fermenters and drying, on a construction contract close to EUR 2 million (scope unclear; opening 2027)

name: Duckweed on aquaculture effluent for feed
what: Duckweed grown on pond or processing effluent, used fresh or dried in fish, poultry or pig feed; a protein concentrate for food later
why_vietnam: Duckweed is already a permitted livestock feed material; warm climate; large aquaculture effluent volumes; a Vietnamese collection of more than 100 wild strains
must_be_true: Yields of 10 to 30 t dry matter per ha per year on Vietnamese sites; heavy-metal and manganese levels within feed limits; low-cost harvesting and drying
kill_tests: Field yields below 10 t per ha per year; contaminants above feed limits on typical effluent
first_customers: Integrated pangasius and tilapia farms; small feed mills; livestock farms
partners: Can Tho University and other aquaculture faculties; pangasius processors

name: High-value, low-dose precision-fermentation ingredients
what: Enzymes, heme or sweet proteins and specialty functional proteins developed by Vietnamese teams and made under contract (Singapore, Thailand, China) until a domestic option exists Version 0.10: low-dose flavour fats fit the same model (a Western brand has its fat made under contract by a Chinese microbial-oil producer); bulk fats do not (section 26.6)

name: Cultivated seafood research
what: Serum-free adaptation of striped catfish and shrimp cells, growth-factor expression and regulatory preparation, in partnership with foreign groups Version 0.10: research tasks now include low-cost hydrolysate media from Vietnamese soy, rice bran or fish by-products, because amino acids, not growth factors, are the larger medium cost in the published model (USD 19 against USD 3 per kg of cells at scale); candidate target species are Asian seabass or grouper, for which food-oriented muscle cell lines were published abroad in 2024 and 2025 (metadata only), with striped catfish as a low-cost model species and shrimp deferred until a continuous line exists

name: Koji and fungal foods on food-grade side streams
what: Solid-state fermented foods and ingredients using characterised Aspergillus oryzae or other food moulds on okara, broken rice or brewer's spent grain
why_vietnam: Tuong (fermented soybean paste) tradition; local gene tools for A. oryzae; koji on food substrates goes through ordinary self-declaration; food-grade side streams exist Version 0.10: a Vietnamese screen of yeasts from fermented foods found isolates with 62 to 67% protein in flasks, without safety data; koji mycelium deli meats from a Berkeley spin-out are sold commercially in the United States (USD 50 million raised by 2023)

kill_tests: Strain safety data cannot be obtained; sensory trials fail with target buyers

name: Mung bean and rice protein for plant drinks
what: Protein concentrates or isolates from mung bean and rice, replacing imported pea protein in high-protein plant drinks and yogurts
why_vietnam: A large plant-milk industry; imported pea protein in high-protein lines; rice and mung bean are familiar; ordinary food rules
must_be_true: Functional and sensory parity in drinks; cost near imported pea protein; a buyer specification; a reliable mung bean supply (65% of imports come from Myanmar); Version 0.10: raw material must fit the price. At 2023 to 2025 import prices, mung beans alone cost USD 3.0 to 4.9 per kg of isolate (60 to 80% protein recovery assumed), above Chinese pea protein at USD 2 to 3 per kg, so the line needs a paid starch co-product or a higher-priced job such as egg-white replacement (TPP-05); rice protein from broken rice costs USD 5.1 to 6.6 per kg of product in raw material alone, so the rice arm works only as a co-product of a rice syrup or starch line, and we found no such line in Vietnam (our calculation)
kill_tests: Buyer rejects on taste or stability; cost above imported pea protein by more than a local-sourcing premium buyers will pay; Version 0.10: no buyer for the mung bean starch co-product at a price that brings raw-material cost inside the TPP-05 band; for the rice arm, no rice syrup or starch host within two years
first_customers: Vinamilk, TH and other plant-milk makers
capital_note: Moderate (wet fractionation and drying; not estimated)
source_ids: FORM-01; FORM-08; SCI-40; SCI-41; SCI-42; SLP-14; SLP-08; SLP-01; FS-26; DIE-12; BUY-09

name: Hybrid fish cakes and fish balls with plant protein
what: Vietnamese fish-cake, fish-ball and fish-tofu makers (chả cá, cá viên, đậu hũ cá) replace 10 to 30% of the fish protein with plant protein (imported soy isolate first; mung bean or rice protein from T10 later), with the fish share printed on the label. Domestic retail and canteens first, then finished-product exports (Japan and the US buy most Vietnamese fish cakes). Not a hybrid frozen surimi: that trade is bought by gel-strength grade
why_vietnam: Surimi and fish-cake exports of more than USD 344 million in 2025 through more than 100 exporters (SLS-01; SLS-03); wild-fish raw material squeezed by the planned capture cut from 3.83 Mt (2025) to 2.8 Mt (2030), the trawler cap and IUU import problems (MAC-15; NTS-08; AQF-15; SLS-04); pangasius side-stream surimi already made commercially (RD-52); plant chả cá chay already on shelves (FORM-01); surimi gel science at Nha Trang University and Can Tho University (SLS-06)
must_be_true: Buyers accept a declared fish share below today's products; sensory panels accept 10 to 30% substitution in Vietnamese formats (panels abroad rejected 30% wheat or rice and 40% soy or pea protein, SLS-07); plant protein stays well below fish protein per kg of protein (3.6 to 7.5 times cheaper in 2025, our calculation with an assumed surimi dry matter); no Korean, Japanese or EU rule blocks fish-plant composites
kill_tests: A sensory panel or the first buyer rejects at 15% substitution; no maker agrees to a trial run within 12 months; the per-kg-protein price gap between surimi and plant protein falls below about 2 times; target export buyers set a minimum fish content above the hybrid level (Korea's premium trend is 80% fish or more, SLS-11)
first_customers: Domestic fish-cake makers (LC Foods, Viet Sin); leading surimi exporters with finished-product lines (DALU SURIMI, CASES, KICOIMEX; finished lines unverified); contract caterers whose menus carry chả cá dishes
partners: Nha Trang University and Can Tho University (surimi gels, sensory panels); soy isolate suppliers; T10 developers for mung bean or rice protein; VASEP surimi committee
capital_note: Formulation and sensory trials on existing bowl-cutter, forming and steaming or frying lines; no new plant. Protein-cost saving about 14 to 17% at 20% substitution before extra binders and any price discount (our calculation). Cost of trials not estimated

name: Domestic food-grade soybean and mung bean for soy foods and plant drinks
what: Contract-grown, non-GM, food-grade soybeans (and in a second step mung beans) sold to soy-milk, tofu and plant-drink makers, replacing part of the imported beans behind the protein people already eat. Step one is a buyer-led value-chain taskforce on the model of the EU fava bean roadmap: a barrier map from seed to buyer, a farm-economics test of two or three farm types (Red River Delta winter crop after rice; upland soybean in Lam Dong (former Dak Nong)), and a price and volume series
why_vietnam: Soy foods carry about 181,000 t of protein a year (2023) on beans that are 97.5% imported, nearly ten times what new routes deliver in 2035 on the benchmark path (DIE-07; ch22). It is the only in-scope route found that raises the domestic-input share of protein people already eat at that scale: the 2010 soybean area (205 kha) at 2.0 to 2.5 t/ha would give 410 to 510 kt of beans, 76% to 95% of 2025 food soybean use (our calculation; AQF-20; MAC-04). A named buyer markets non-GM and breeds for it: Vinasoy holds 2,072 soybean lines and VINASOY 05 yields above 2.5 t/ha at Cu Jut; its parent plans to invest in soybean raw-material areas in 2026 (AIB-06). Consumers pay a large premium for non-GM soy milk (NOV-08). Land is being released from rice (654 kha by 2030; NTS-15), and MAE asks to reduce import dependence through domestic raw-material areas (SEC-02)
must_be_true: A farm margin for soybean in rotation at least equal to maize or vegetables at a price buyers will pay; buyers pay a premium over imported non-GM food beans that covers the gap (domestic 25,000 to 30,000 VND/kg against 13,000 to 15,000 for imports in 2024, AQF-20; or 1.4 to 1.7 times the 2023 Canadian import unit value of USD 686/t, our calculation from SEC-05); contract yields of 2.0 t/ha or more against a national average of about 1.3 t/ha (PCV-007); drying, storage and grading capacity near growing areas
kill_tests: The farm-economics test shows soybean below maize or rice margins at any price buyers accept; Vinasoy and two tofu or plant-drink makers will not sign conditional contracts for at least 5,000 t a year (our threshold); imported identity-preserved non-GM beans land at under two thirds of the domestic contract price for two years running; contract yields stay below 2.0 t/ha over three seasons
first_customers: Vinasoy (soy milk); ToFu House and other industrial tofu makers; plant-drink makers looking for local mung bean (T10 buyers such as Vinamilk)
partners: Vinasoy Soybean Applied Research Centre (VSAC); MAE crop and extension agencies; provinces releasing rice land; Can Tho University and other groups that study rice-upland rotations (our suggestion; not contacted)
horizon: 1 to 5 years (farm-economics test and taskforce in year 1; contract areas in years 2 to 5)
capital_note: Low fixed capital: seed multiplication, extension, drying and storage near growing areas, and working capital for crop purchase. Not costed; the farm-economics test sets the size. Best owned by the buyer (contract farming) with public extension and seed support, not venture capital

name: Characterised Vietnamese food-strain set
what: Characterise 20 to 50 moulds and yeasts already used in Vietnamese ferments and held in public collections (Aspergillus oryzae from tuong; Rhizopus and Amylomyces from banh men; protein-rich yeasts such as Pichia kudriavzevii isolates): whole-genome sequence, toxin-gene and antibiotic-resistance screens, growth on cassava glucose and okara, protein content; publish the data and supply the strains on one standard licence with pre-agreed benefit-sharing terms under the Decree 43/2026 route
why_vietnam: VTCC holds over 15,000 strains, 3,869 documented and available to domestic users (SLF-01); 41 works on microbes of Vietnamese ferments but none on food-strain safety characterisation (SLF-03); a Vietnamese screen found a yeast with 62 to 67% protein and no safety data (SLF-04); Decree 43/2026 cut the access licence to about 19 working days at provincial level, but benefit sharing of at least 1% of product revenue still applies (SLF-02; REG-60); T9's first kill test is strain safety data; strains with a history of use in Vietnamese food fit P1's traditional-food lane
